item.title: Arabica Coffee Prices Hit Record on U.S., Colombia Tariff Spat
item.description: Arabica coffee prices hit a record level, as traders digested the withdrawal of President Trump’s threats to impose tariffs and economic sanctions on Colombia.

item.description: Gain insight on Experian, SoFi Technologies and more in the latest Market Talks covering Financial Services.

item.description: Panic fueling the selloff of Nvidia, Broadcom and other tech giants is overblown.

item.title: Comex Gold, Silver Settle Lower
item.description: Gold settled 1.4% lower, down two of the past three sessions, and silver fell 2.5%, down three of the past four sessions.

item.title: Stocks Sink in Broad AI Rout Sparked by China's DeepSeek
item.description: U.S. stocks were mostly lower, with the Nasdaq leading declines as makers of AI infrastructure suffered steep falls, many in the double digits. Nvidia was down 16%.

item.title: When it came to Cal AI’s viral success, a small army of influencers paid off
item.description: The company generated over $30 million in revenue in two years and was acquired by MyFitnessPal for an undisclosed amount of money in March.

item.title: Tesla reveals SpaceX-powered Roadster that flies and falls with style
item.description: The new car used thrusters to leap over a Cybercab, Cybertruck, Tesla Semi, Model Y, and Model 3 at a demo in Texas.

item.title: Even Benchmark thinks AI is eroding the venture pact against backing rivals
item.description: Benchmark says the Valley’s rule against backing rivals is getting harder to keep.

item.title: Replit’s CEO says the future of work is the ‘self-driving company’
item.description: Replit CEO Amjad Masad envisions a future of “self-driving companies,” where AI agents handle day-to-day tasks and people focus on higher-level decisions.

item.title: Veritas expands its anti-counterfeit chip to jewelry, trophies, and fragrance bottles
item.description: Counterfeiters are getting better at replicating brands' marks and passing off dupes, known as "superfakes," as genuine items. A startup called Veritas wants to tackle the problem with its own chip that verifies goods.

item.title: Mark Wahlberg on using AI in film ‘the right way’ and being open to an AI clone carrying on his legacy
item.description: Actor and angel investor Mark Wahlberg says he's OK with using AI in filmmaking, provided it's used "to enhance what you're doing."

item.title: Jev is Vercel’s fastest-adopted AI model ever
item.description: The data comes from Vercel's AI gateway, a unified API service similar to OpenRouter.

item.title: In ‘You Can See Everything,’ Elizabeth Holmes meets her equal in comedian Nathan Fielder
item.description: Nathan Fielder's documentary about disgraced Theranos CEO Elizabeth Holmes has created a constellation of colliding personas that interrogate the very nature of authenticity.

item.title: Tressfecta wants to make hair braiding a less arduous task for hairstylists
item.description: Tressfecta builds products for textured hair. Its first project is a tool called Plait Pilot that helps braiders with the initial process of separating hair from packs before braiding begins.

item.title: Elorian’s first AI model wants to reason with images, not just about them
item.description: According to Elorian's evaluations, Glimpse outperforms even GPT-6 Astra on scientific chart reasoning and short-form video captioning, with competitive results on other visual reasoning tasks.

item.title: Waymo’s robotaxis are headed to Canada
item.description: The company will start off by testing its self-driving vehicles on Toronto's streets.

item.title: India becomes the latest country to report rogue AI agent activity
item.description: The agents got in through credentials and connection settings left exposed in app configurations, public code repositories, and overly permissive cloud roles.

item.title: Porsche’s electric Macan Turbo is an automotive existential crisis
item.description: The 2026 Porsche Macan Turbo EV is a two-row crossover with 630 horsepower and a 100-kilowatt-hour battery.

item.title: Replit is no longer working with Anthropic, CEO says
item.description: Masad said the decision was made for a number of different reasons, including cost. Replit announced a partnership with OpenAI in August, but there was never any indication that it was no longer with Anthropic.
